evidence: Inherited shared-template isolation defect, not a task-local alteration. Agent Dockerfile copies only instructions/assets (14-15) and initializes an empty app; task.toml:28 selects a separate verifier. tests/Dockerfile:43-44 protects /tests and test.sh:3,10-12 protects logs/tests. test.sh:104-111 launches the submission with sanitized env and uid/gid 65534; 207-209 starts RewardKit without a separate PID namespace. Installed pinned harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7 agents.py:145-148 places the entire judge prompt directly in `claude -p <prompt>` argv. The disposable --network none probe used that real command builder with an inert CLI stand-in and recovered its complete prompt through /proc/<root-pid>/cmdline as uid 65534. Result: full_prompt_recovered=true, private_tests_denied=true, reward_write_denied=true, app_env_has_provider_variables=false. Thus filesystem protection is effective, but criteria can still reach submitted code through process metadata. No credentials were printed or provider calls made. Probe source SHA256=cd81ee34168a728d0ad1bad15b4d04701e6c0926903d4a14036faee3b8d853df; result SHA256=f857671f7c2fd5139b12dcb1555f17442b38a43ca12ccd29d8b6c0e93e805ffd. All five task/template comparisons (agent Dockerfile, verifier Dockerfile, test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py) were byte-identical. The 21 indexed scripted-product artifacts all matched their hashes, but provide no configured-judge isolation proof. Scope is an installed-library/OS boundary test, not a full hosted judge exploit or measured score.
counterexample: A submitted server can poll /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline after the judge starts, locate the claude -p argument and learn exact private criteria/probes despite being uid 65534 and unable to open /tests. A weak implementation can adapt its responses to those probes; no high-score claim was measured. The conforming alternative is an ordinary app using /app and /assets: the controls show private tests/reward access is denied as intended, with no demonstrated false-fail for such an app.
suggested_fix: Escalate to the shared-harness owner to isolate the app PID/proc view from judge processes or keep private prompts out of app-readable argv; retain the mandated task/template bytes unchanged under the current authorization.
